short: The German surrender took effect and the war in Europe ended after five years and eight months.
full:
Jodl signed the instrument of unconditional surrender at Eisenhower's headquarters in Reims at 2.41am on 7 May 1945, to take effect at 11.01pm on the 8th. Stalin objected that a capitulation of that magnitude should be made in Berlin to the Soviet high command, and a second signing took place there late on 8 May, by which time it was already 9 May in Moscow. Russia and much of eastern Europe have kept Victory Day on 9 May ever since.

Crowds filled Whitehall and Times Square, and the lights went back on in London for the first time since 1939. What the celebrations concealed was less cheerful: a continent with some 40 million dead, eleven million displaced persons in Germany alone, cities without roofs or food distribution, and Allied armies facing one another along a line that hardened into the Iron Curtain. The war against Japan still had four months to run, and the occupation of Germany would last a great deal longer.
